According to the document "Valuation of Surface Coatings in High-Energy Density Lithium-ion Battery Cathode Materials" (ensm-2021), page 10:

The LLTO coated NCM materials exhibited improved rate capability, as shown in Fig. 7 (d). This increase in rate capability is attributed to high ionic conductivity of the LLTO coating layer and suppression of undesirable side reactions between the electrolyte and the cathode surface due to the presence of the coating layer.

The cycling performance of LLTO coated NCM also drastically improved when cycled at 0.5C as shown in Fig. 7 (e). The pristine NCM only retained 56.6% of its initial discharge capacity after 200 cycles. On the other hand, LLTO coated NCM retained about 85.5%, 57.2% and 86.2% for LLTO-0.5, LLTO-1 and LLTO-2 respectively.

The 2 mol.% coating lowered the rate capability, which may be due to the increase in the thickness of the coating layer, resulting in the suppression of electron transfer process during charge/discharge cycling.

The LLTO-1 coating retained the most capacity after 200 cycles at 0.5C, compared to the pristine NCM.
